definitions.explanation: The punctuation marks ( ) used to enclose supplementary information. The most common type of bracket in Japanese writing.

examples.japanese: {丸括弧|まるかっこ}の{中|なか}に{注|ちゅう}を{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please put the note inside parentheses.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}み{方|かた}は{丸括弧|まるかっこ}で{示|しめ}されている。
examples.english: The reading is shown in parentheses.

examples.japanese: {数学|すうがく}では、{丸括弧|まるかっこ}は{計算|けいさん}の{順序|じゅんじょ}を{表|あらわ}すのに{使|つか}う。
examples.english: In mathematics, parentheses are used to indicate the order of operations.

notes:
Composed of {丸|まる} (round, circle) + {括弧|かっこ} (brackets). The standard term for the round brackets ( ) in Japanese. In everyday speech, people often just say {括弧|かっこ}, which defaults to parentheses unless another type is specified.

JAPANESE BRACKET TYPES:
- {丸括弧|まるかっこ}: parentheses ( )
- {角括弧|かくかっこ}: square brackets [ ]
- {中括弧|なかかっこ}: curly brackets { }
- {山括弧|やまかっこ}: angle brackets < >
- {隅付|すみつ}き{括弧|かっこ}: lenticular brackets (thick square brackets used in Japanese typesetting)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸括弧|まるかっこ}で{囲|かこ}む: to enclose in parentheses
- {丸括弧|まるかっこ}を{付|つ}ける: to add parentheses
- {丸括弧|まるかっこ}{内|ない}: inside the parentheses

USAGE NOTE:
In Japanese text, full-width parentheses are standard. When dictating, people say {括弧|かっこ} to open and {括弧閉|かっこと}じ to close.
